name: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
authors: Guanzhi Wang, Yuqi Xie, Yunfan Jiang, Ajay Mandlekar, Chaowei Xiao, Yuke Zhu, Linxi 'Jim' Fan, Anima Anandkumar et al. (NVIDIA; Caltech; UT Austin; Stanford; UW-Madison)
venue: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR) 2024; also certified at ICLR 2025 Journal Track. First arXiv preprint May 2023 (arXiv:2305.16291).
reflection_type: tool-verified + verbal-self-critique. Iterative prompting with three feedback channels: (1) environment feedback (e.g. 'I need 7 more iron ingots'), (2) execution errors from the code interpreter, and (3) a separate self-verification GPT-4 'critic' agent that checks task success and, on failure, produces a textual critique on how to complete the task. The authors argue this is more comprehensive than Reflexion's self-reflection because it both checks success and reflects on mistakes.
feedback_source: external-tool (Minecraft/Mineflayer environment feedback + program-interpreter execution errors) combined with self-generated signal (a separate GPT-4 instance acting as a self-verification critic). No human-labeled ground truth in the main loop (humans only used optionally for 3D-building multimodal feedback).
iteration_structure: iterative-refine within a task (regenerate/refine code each round incorporating environment feedback, execution errors, and critique) with episodic-retry-with-reset across tasks: if the agent is stuck after 4 rounds of code generation, the automatic curriculum is queried for another task and the failed task can be re-attempted later. Lifelong loop: curriculum -> code generation/refinement -> self-verification -> add skill to library.
reflection_object: Primarily the agent's own code/skill (executable JavaScript program for a task) which is iteratively refined and then stored. Also the action trajectory/plan and the curriculum context (completed/failed task list). The most distinctive object is the reusable skill (executable code) added to an ever-growing skill library, plus reasoning chains (chain-of-thought before code generation).
requires_training: none (no model parameter fine-tuning; GPT-4 accessed via blackbox API queries). Learning is purely in-context via prompting and an external skill library + curriculum.
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge: a separate instantiated GPT-4 agent acts as a self-verification critic that decides task success/failure and gives a critique. No trained reward model; partial verifiable signal comes from the environment/interpreter (execution errors, environment state).
distillation_target: reusable-skill/workflow. Successful refined behaviors are distilled into executable code skills stored in a vector-database skill library, indexed by the GPT-3.5-generated embedding of each skill's description; retrieved (top-5) and composed for new tasks, compounding capability and alleviating catastrophic forgetting.
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered. The reflective/self-improving behavior is produced by an engineered multi-prompt scaffold (automatic curriculum + skill library + iterative prompting with self-verification critic) wrapped around a frozen GPT-4, not by RL-emergent reflection in the model weights.
memory_type: skill-library (vector database of executable code skills, key = embedding of program description, value = program) plus short-term scratchpad context (current state, last-round code, feedback) and a curriculum-level record of completed/failed tasks.
memory_persistence: cross-task and cross-episode within a lifelong run; the skill library is also shown to transfer cross-world (zero-shot generalization in a new Minecraft world, and even plug-and-play into AutoGPT). Not framed as a cross-session production deployment.
memory_curation_mechanism: append-only with refinement before insertion: a new skill is only added after self-verification confirms task success, and skills are iteratively refined before storage; skills can be overwritten/updated when a function with the same task is regenerated. Growth is bounded by retrieval-gating (top-5 relevant skills retrieved by embedding similarity rather than dumping the whole library into context).
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level for self-verification (did the task succeed?) combined with block-level/line-level for code (execution errors and environment feedback localize the failing operation, e.g. missing ingredients or invalid item, enabling targeted code fixes). Effectively step/block-level within a code skill.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: both. Intra-task: iterative refinement of a single skill's code within up to 4 rounds. Inter-task: experience transfer across tasks via the persistent skill library and the curriculum's record of past successes/failures, enabling compositional reuse and generalization to new tasks/worlds.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mix of mid-trajectory-recovery and avoidance: within a task it recovers in-flight by fixing code using environment/error/critique feedback (post-hoc revision of the generated program each round); across tasks, if stuck after 4 rounds it avoids by moving to a new curriculum task and may re-attempt the failed task later.
task_domains: embodied/games (open-ended Minecraft lifelong learning), with code generation (executable JavaScript skills) and tool-use/decision-making as the underlying mechanism.
benchmarks: MineDojo / Minecraft (via Mineflayer JavaScript API). Custom evaluation axes rather than a standard NLP benchmark: number of unique items discovered, Minecraft tech-tree mastery (wooden->stone->iron->diamond tools), map traversal distance, and zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks (Diamond Pickaxe, Golden Sword, Lava Bucket, Compass) in a new world.
headline_result: Using a frozen GPT-4 (gpt-4-0314) with no fine-tuning, Voyager obtains 3.3x more unique items (63 unique items within 160 prompting iterations; the TMLR camera-ready states 3.1x), travels 2.3x longer distances, and unlocks key tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA, and is the only method to unlock the diamond tier (1/3 trials). It also generalizes its learned skill library zero-shot to a new world, solving novel tasks that all baselines fail.
baselines: ReAct (Yao et al. 2022), Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023), and AutoGPT — all re-interpreted/re-implemented to run in MineDojo with the same environment feedback and agent-state observations. Internal ablation baselines: Voyager w/o Skill Library, random/manual curriculum, removing each feedback type (environment feedback, execution errors, self-verification), and GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 for code generation.
gains_vs_baseline: Tech tree (avg prompting iterations over 3 trials, fewer is better): Voyager reaches wooden in 6+/-2, stone 11+/-2, iron 21+/-7, diamond 102 (1/3); AutoGPT reaches wooden 92+/-72, stone 94+/-72, iron 135+/-103, never diamond; ReAct and Reflexion fail all tiers (0/3). => ~15.3x faster wooden, 8.5x stone, 6.4x iron vs strongest baseline. Exploration: 63 unique items, 3.3x AutoGPT (the next best). Zero-shot generalization: Voyager solves all 4 unseen tasks (3/3 each, e.g. Diamond Pickaxe 19+/-3 iters), while ReAct/Reflexion/AutoGPT solve none within 50 iters; adding Voyager's skill library to AutoGPT lets it solve some tasks (plug-and-play boost).
compute_cost_profile: No gradient training (zero training cost; GPT-4 used only via API). Inference cost is the dominant cost: multi-agent, multi-round prompting (curriculum + code-gen with up to 4 refinement rounds + a separate self-verification GPT-4 agent + GPT-3.5 for self-ask/embeddings), so many GPT-4 calls per skill. Authors explicitly flag GPT-4 cost as a limitation: GPT-4 is ~15x more expensive than GPT-3.5, but GPT-3.5/open-source LLMs cannot provide the required code-generation quality (GPT-4 yields 5.7x more unique items than GPT-3.5 in ablation).
known_limitations: Cost: GPT-4 API is expensive (~15x GPT-3.5) and the quality jump is required. Inaccuracies: agent can get stuck and fail to generate a correct skill; the self-verification module occasionally fails (e.g. not recognizing spider string as a success signal for beating a spider). Hallucinations: the automatic curriculum sometimes proposes non-existent/unachievable tasks (e.g. craft a 'copper sword'), and code generation hallucinates invalid game facts (e.g. using cobblestone as fuel) or calls non-existent control-primitive APIs, causing execution errors. No visual/multimodal perception in the main system (GPT-4 was text-only at the time).
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier plus self-verify, but NOT ground-truth-oracle. Success is judged by a self-verification GPT-4 critic (self-verify) augmented by deterministic environment feedback and interpreter execution errors (external tool/verifier). No human-labeled oracle in the loop; the environment provides partially verifiable state but final task-success judgement is LLM-self-judged, so it can err.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive in this setting: ablations show self-verification is the single most important feedback type (removing it drops discovered item count by 73%), and the iterative environment/error feedback meaningfully improves program synthesis. Efficacy is supported by the strong verifiable/environment signal; the self-judged success check is imperfect and occasionally wrong.
calibration_effect: not-measured (paper predates the reasoning-model 'overconfidence' literature and does not report calibration metrics).
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (Voyager is a self-evolving agent, not a failure-attribution method). Within itself it does classify task success/failure and produce a corrective critique, and execution errors localize the failing code operation, but it does not formally attribute failures across agents or steps as a taxonomy.
failure_mode_addressed: Targets catastrophic forgetting (via compositional skill library), inability to recover from execution errors (via interpreter-error feedback), and poor open-ended exploration / getting stuck (via automatic curriculum and self-verification deciding when to move on or retry). Relative to MAST-style modes, it mitigates 'premature termination' and aims past 'superficial self-reflection' by combining success-checking with reflective critique; it itself can still suffer from hallucination and superficial/incorrect self-verification.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new benchmark dataset; built on the existing MineDojo/Mineflayer Minecraft environment. The team open-sourced the full codebase and all prompts (https://github.com/MineDojo/Voyager), and the learned skill library is reusable/plug-and-play.
builds_on: Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) and ReAct (Yao et al. 2022) for verbal self-reflection/reasoning+acting; MineDojo (Fan et al. 2022) and Mineflayer for the Minecraft environment/API; DreamCoder (Ellis et al. 2020) for the program-as-skill / library-learning idea; chain-of-thought prompting (Wei et al. 2022); GPT-4 (OpenAI 2023). Contrasts with RL/imitation Minecraft agents (VPT, DreamerV3, MineDojo) and LLM planners (GITM, DEPS/Describe-Explain-Plan-Select, Plan4MC).
extended_by_or_inspired: Inspired and is frequently compared against later open-world / lifelong-agent and skill/workflow-memory works, e.g. JARVIS-1 (memory-augmented multimodal Minecraft agent, 2023), GITM (Ghost in the Minecraft), ExpeL (experiential learning), and Agent Workflow Memory (AWM) and other 'skill library / reusable workflow' agent methods; widely cited as the canonical executable-skill-library self-evolving agent.
citation_count: ~1,406 (Semantic Scholar, as fetched 2026-06-08); Google Scholar reports ~1,914.
reasoning_model_native: no. Voyager wraps a frozen non-reasoning GPT-4 (gpt-4-0314) with an external scaffold; reflection is engineered via prompting, not native to an o1/R1-style reasoning model. The approach is in principle model-agnostic given a capable code-generating backbone.
on_policy_distillation_link: Conceptually related to skill/experience distillation: refined on-policy rollouts (successful, self-verified executable skills) are distilled into a retrievable skill library that improves future behavior. However, it is in-context only (no weight updates / no on-policy gradient distillation), so it is an in-context analogue rather than true on-policy distillation.
sample_efficiency: High in trials-to-milestone terms vs baselines: reaches wooden tool in ~6 prompting iterations, stone ~11, iron ~21 (vs AutoGPT 92/94/135), and solves unseen tasks in ~18-21 iterations (3/3) where baselines fail within 50. Each 'iteration' is a multi-call GPT-4 round (up to 4 code-gen rounds per task), so API-call cost per skill is non-trivial.
